notice: Original Canonical Cloud readiness prompts. Not exhaustive normative controls, certification, legal advice, a completed regulatory questionnaire, or independent assurance. Complete each framework independently.

frameworks.title: SOC 2
frameworks.scopeNote: Select Type I or Type II, service boundaries, reporting period and applicable trust services categories with the CPA. This is not a SOC report.

questions.prompt: Have you agreed the service boundary, report type, categories and examination period?
questions.evidence: Engagement scope and category selection.

questions.prompt: Does the system description identify commitments, components, dependencies and customer responsibilities?
questions.evidence: Versioned system description and service commitments.

questions.prompt: Can leadership demonstrate ownership, oversight and escalation of control failures?
questions.evidence: Governance minutes, role assignments and escalation examples.

questions.prompt: Are service risks assessed and linked to operating controls and remediation owners?
questions.evidence: Risk register and treatment decisions.

questions.prompt: Do joiner, mover, leaver and privileged-access samples support the access policy?
questions.evidence: Dated access approvals and revocation samples.

questions.prompt: Can sampled production changes be traced through approval, testing and deployment?
questions.evidence: Change population and independently selected samples.

questions.prompt: Are monitoring alerts investigated and incidents escalated according to commitments?
questions.evidence: Alert tickets, incident records and response exercise.

questions.prompt: Are relevant subservice organizations evaluated and their responsibilities explicitly addressed?
questions.evidence: Supplier reviews, reports and complementary controls.

questions.prompt: Do recovery and processing tests support the selected availability or integrity commitments?
questions.evidence: Restore results and processing reconciliation samples.

questions.prompt: Have control exceptions and evidence gaps been reviewed across the intended reporting period?
questions.evidence: Exception log, sample rationale and remediation retests.

frameworks.title: NIST Cybersecurity Framework
frameworks.scopeNote: Use Current and Target Profiles appropriate to the organization. A Profile or Tier is not certification or a universal maturity score.

questions.prompt: Are the organizational context, critical services and Current Profile documented?
questions.evidence: Scope, stakeholder needs and Current Profile.

questions.prompt: Are cybersecurity strategy, responsibilities and risk tolerance approved by leadership?
questions.evidence: Governance charter and risk appetite decisions.

questions.prompt: Does the asset inventory identify owners, dependencies and sensitive information?
questions.evidence: Hardware, software, service and data inventories.

questions.prompt: Are threat and vulnerability assessments used to prioritize the Target Profile?
questions.evidence: Risk analysis and prioritized Target Profile gaps.

questions.prompt: Are supplier security expectations established and monitored throughout the relationship?
questions.evidence: Supplier requirements, due diligence and monitoring.

questions.prompt: Have access, authentication and workforce-awareness protections been tested?
questions.evidence: Access samples, authentication configurations and training records.

questions.prompt: Do protective configurations, maintenance and backups cover critical services?
questions.evidence: Configuration baselines, patch evidence and restore tests.

questions.prompt: Can detection processes identify and triage adverse events?
questions.evidence: Telemetry coverage and alert-triage exercise.

questions.prompt: Have incident response and recovery plans been exercised with responsible participants?
questions.evidence: Exercise timeline, communications and recovery outcomes.

questions.prompt: Are Profile gaps assigned, resourced, measured and reassessed after material changes?
questions.evidence: Improvement plan, owners and review cadence.

frameworks.title: ISO/IEC 27001
frameworks.scopeNote: Use the licensed standard and an agreed ISMS scope. Original prompts do not reproduce Annex A or substitute for certification audits.

questions.prompt: Is the ISMS scope justified against business context and interested-party requirements?
questions.evidence: Approved scope, context analysis and requirements register.

questions.prompt: Has leadership assigned security responsibilities and measurable ISMS objectives?
questions.evidence: Policy approval, responsibilities and objective measures.

questions.prompt: Is the information-security risk assessment method consistently applied?
questions.evidence: Risk criteria, asset scope and assessment records.

questions.prompt: Are treatment decisions and the Statement of Applicability justified and maintained?
questions.evidence: Risk treatment plan and licensed-control applicability record.

questions.prompt: Are competence, awareness and controlled documentation maintained for the ISMS?
questions.evidence: Competence records and document control history.

questions.prompt: Do sampled operations demonstrate that selected controls are implemented?
questions.evidence: Operational samples linked to selected controls.

questions.prompt: Are supplier and change-related information-security risks managed?
questions.evidence: Supplier assessments and change risk reviews.

questions.prompt: Has an impartial internal audit covered the scoped ISMS?
questions.evidence: Audit program, competence, workpapers and findings.

questions.prompt: Does management review assess performance, changes and improvement opportunities?
questions.evidence: Management review inputs, minutes and decisions.

questions.prompt: Are corrective actions effective, and has climate-change relevance been considered?
questions.evidence: Root-cause retests and documented context consideration.

frameworks.title: EU GDPR
frameworks.scopeNote: Determine territorial scope, controller/processor roles and applicable national rules with privacy counsel. Readiness is not a legal compliance opinion.

questions.prompt: Have processing activities, purposes, data flows and controller/processor roles been mapped?
questions.evidence: Processing inventory and role determinations.

questions.prompt: Is a defensible lawful basis recorded for each purpose, including sensitive-data conditions?
questions.evidence: Purpose-level basis analysis and consent records.

questions.prompt: Do notices accurately explain actual processing and required rights information?
questions.evidence: Published notices and processing-to-notice reconciliation.

questions.prompt: Can requests for applicable individual rights be authenticated and fulfilled?
questions.evidence: Rights-request procedure and timed case samples.

questions.prompt: Are collection limits, retention periods and deletion procedures enforced?
questions.evidence: Retention schedule, minimization decisions and deletion tests.

questions.prompt: Are processor contracts and subprocessors controlled for the actual services?
questions.evidence: Processing agreements, instructions and subprocessor records.

questions.prompt: Have international transfers and the relevant safeguards been assessed?
questions.evidence: Transfer inventory, mechanism and supporting assessment.

questions.prompt: Are security measures proportionate to personal-data risks and regularly reviewed?
questions.evidence: Security risk assessment and effectiveness tests.

questions.prompt: Are high-risk processing, DPIA duties and DPO requirements assessed?
questions.evidence: Screening decisions, DPIAs and responsibility assignments.

questions.prompt: Can personal-data breaches be assessed, documented and notified when required?
questions.evidence: Breach decision log and notification exercise.

frameworks.title: HIPAA
frameworks.scopeNote: Determine covered-entity/business-associate status and applicable Privacy, Security and Breach Notification duties. Proposed rule changes are not assumed effective.

questions.prompt: Are regulated roles and all locations of PHI and ePHI identified?
questions.evidence: Role determination and PHI/ePHI data-flow inventory.

questions.prompt: Does the risk analysis cover all scoped ePHI and relevant threats?
questions.evidence: Current risk analysis, methodology and completeness review.

questions.prompt: Are risk treatment decisions and addressable-specification rationales documented?
questions.evidence: Risk management plan and reasoned safeguard decisions.

questions.prompt: Are security responsibility, workforce training and sanction procedures established?
questions.evidence: Assigned officials, training samples and workforce procedures.

questions.prompt: Are workforce access authorization and termination controls effective?
questions.evidence: Access approvals, unique identities and termination samples.

questions.prompt: Do facility, workstation and device/media safeguards protect ePHI?
questions.evidence: Physical review, device controls and disposal evidence.

questions.prompt: Do technical safeguards address access, integrity, auditability and transmission risks?
questions.evidence: Configuration evidence and audit-control test results.

questions.prompt: Can contingency procedures restore ePHI and sustain critical operations?
questions.evidence: Backup, recovery and emergency-mode exercise records.

questions.prompt: Are business-associate arrangements and privacy-use restrictions operational?
questions.evidence: Business-associate agreements and disclosure procedures.

questions.prompt: Can suspected breaches be investigated and required notifications coordinated?
questions.evidence: Incident-to-breach workflow and notification exercise.

frameworks.title: PCI DSS
frameworks.scopeNote: Confirm cardholder-data scope and SAQ/ROC eligibility with the acquirer or payment brands. This is not an official SAQ, ROC or attestation.

questions.prompt: Are payment flows, the cardholder-data environment and scope-reducing claims validated?
questions.evidence: Payment diagrams, inventories and segmentation evidence.

questions.prompt: Are network boundaries and secure configurations maintained and tested?
questions.evidence: Network rule reviews and configuration samples.

questions.prompt: Are stored account data, retention and cryptographic keys appropriately controlled?
questions.evidence: Data discovery, retention and key-management records.

questions.prompt: Are transmissions over relevant networks protected and monitored?
questions.evidence: Transport configurations and certificate review.

questions.prompt: Are malware defenses and secure development practices operating?
questions.evidence: Defense coverage and development security samples.

questions.prompt: Do access restrictions, identity controls and applicable MFA requirements work?
questions.evidence: Role reviews and authentication test results.

questions.prompt: Are physical access and visitor handling appropriate to payment systems?
questions.evidence: Access logs and physical inspection records.

questions.prompt: Can audit logs support investigation and timely response?
questions.evidence: Log coverage, retention and investigation samples.

questions.prompt: Are vulnerability scans, penetration tests and payment-page protections assessed where applicable?
questions.evidence: Authorized test reports and relevant payment-page evidence.

questions.prompt: Are service providers, targeted risk analyses and incident duties documented?
questions.evidence: Responsibility matrix, risk analyses and incident exercise.

frameworks.title: CIS Critical Security Controls
frameworks.scopeNote: Select an Implementation Group and use the current CIS assessment specification. Original prompts are not a safeguard-by-safeguard CIS attestation.

questions.prompt: Is the selected Implementation Group justified for organizational risk and resources?
questions.evidence: Implementation Group rationale and scoped safeguard list.

questions.prompt: Are enterprise assets and installed software inventoried and reconciled?
questions.evidence: Inventories and unauthorized-asset handling samples.

questions.prompt: Are data inventories, handling requirements and protection measures enforced?
questions.evidence: Data classification and protection evidence.

questions.prompt: Are secure configurations and vulnerability remediation maintained?
questions.evidence: Baseline checks, vulnerability backlog and remediation samples.

questions.prompt: Are account lifecycle and access-control practices consistently applied?
questions.evidence: Account reviews and privilege-removal tests.

questions.prompt: Do audit logging and monitoring cover important security events?
questions.evidence: Log sources, retention and event-review samples.

questions.prompt: Are browser, email, malware and network defenses configured effectively?
questions.evidence: Defense configurations and controlled test results.

questions.prompt: Can recovery procedures restore critical services and information?
questions.evidence: Backup inventory and restoration exercise.

questions.prompt: Are personnel, service providers and application-development risks addressed?
questions.evidence: Training, provider reviews and development evidence.

questions.prompt: Do incident exercises and authorized penetration tests feed measured improvements?
questions.evidence: Exercise findings, test scope and retest results.

frameworks.title: CSA Cloud Controls Matrix
frameworks.scopeNote: Select cloud services and shared responsibilities. This is an original readiness questionnaire, not a completed CAIQ or a STAR certification.

questions.prompt: Are cloud service boundaries and provider/customer responsibilities explicit?
questions.evidence: Service inventory and shared-responsibility matrix.

questions.prompt: Are cloud governance, assurance and risk-management roles established?
questions.evidence: Governance decisions and cloud risk register.

questions.prompt: Are data location, lifecycle and privacy obligations understood?
questions.evidence: Data-flow, residency and deletion evidence.

questions.prompt: Are cloud identities, privileged roles and cryptographic keys controlled?
questions.evidence: Role reviews, key ownership and access tests.

questions.prompt: Do infrastructure, virtualization and tenant-isolation controls match the service model?
questions.evidence: Architecture, isolation tests and configuration evidence.

questions.prompt: Are application interfaces and workload changes developed and deployed securely?
questions.evidence: API inventory and secure delivery samples.

questions.prompt: Are monitoring, vulnerability handling and incident coordination effective?
questions.evidence: Cloud telemetry coverage and incident exercise.

questions.prompt: Are business continuity and portability or exit arrangements tested?
questions.evidence: Recovery, export and service-exit exercises.

questions.prompt: Are suppliers, facilities and organizational personnel covered by assurance activities?
questions.evidence: Supplier assessments and operational assurance records.

questions.prompt: Are proposed CAIQ answers independently substantiated for this specific offering?
questions.evidence: Question-level evidence and reviewer notes.

frameworks.title: ISO/IEC 27701
frameworks.scopeNote: Use the 2025 PIMS requirements and determine PII-controller/processor roles. Do not silently treat the withdrawn 2019 edition as current.

questions.prompt: Are the privacy management system scope and PII roles documented?
questions.evidence: PIMS scope and role inventory.

questions.prompt: Are privacy obligations and interested-party expectations tracked?
questions.evidence: Obligations register and stakeholder analysis.

questions.prompt: Has leadership assigned privacy responsibilities and measurable objectives?
questions.evidence: Governance records and privacy objectives.

questions.prompt: Are privacy risks assessed and treatment decisions recorded?
questions.evidence: Privacy risk assessments and treatment plan.

questions.prompt: Are processing purposes, data categories and information flows maintained?
questions.evidence: Processing records and data-flow review.

questions.prompt: Do operational procedures implement relevant controller obligations?
questions.evidence: Controller procedure samples and rights handling.

questions.prompt: Do processor practices follow authorized instructions and supplier obligations?
questions.evidence: Processor instructions, contracts and subprocessor checks.

questions.prompt: Are sharing, transfer, retention and deletion practices evidenced?
questions.evidence: Transfer records and retention/deletion tests.

questions.prompt: Have privacy incidents, competence and awareness been evaluated?
questions.evidence: Incident exercise and competence records.

questions.prompt: Do internal audit, management review and corrective actions improve the PIMS?
questions.evidence: Audit workpapers, review decisions and retests.

frameworks.title: ISO/IEC 42001
frameworks.scopeNote: Define the AI management system scope and organizational role. This is not AI safety certification or a substitute for applicable AI laws.

questions.prompt: Are scoped AI systems, organizational roles and affected stakeholders identified?
questions.evidence: AI inventory and management-system scope.

questions.prompt: Are AI policy, accountability and objectives approved by leadership?
questions.evidence: Policy, role assignments and measurable objectives.

questions.prompt: Are AI risks and potential impacts assessed across the lifecycle?
questions.evidence: Risk and impact assessments with review history.

questions.prompt: Are treatment controls selected and their applicability justified?
questions.evidence: Treatment plan and control applicability rationale.

questions.prompt: Are data provenance, quality and authorized use documented?
questions.evidence: Data documentation and quality evaluation samples.

questions.prompt: Are development, evaluation and release decisions reproducible?
questions.evidence: Evaluation plans, results and release approvals.

questions.prompt: Are human oversight, user information and escalation mechanisms operational?
questions.evidence: Oversight procedure and escalation exercises.

questions.prompt: Are third-party AI components and dependencies evaluated?
questions.evidence: Supplier evaluations and responsibility agreements.

questions.prompt: Are deployed systems monitored for changing risks and incidents?
questions.evidence: Monitoring criteria and incident/change records.

questions.prompt: Do internal audit, management review and corrective action improve the system?
questions.evidence: Audit findings, management decisions and retests.

frameworks.title: NIST SP 800-53
frameworks.scopeNote: Select and tailor the applicable baseline; the full control catalog is not automatically required for every organization. No federal authorization is implied.

questions.prompt: Are system boundaries, information types and baseline-selection decisions documented?
questions.evidence: System inventory and categorization/tailoring rationale.

questions.prompt: Are applicable controls and organization-defined parameters explicitly selected?
questions.evidence: Tailored baseline and parameter assignments.

questions.prompt: Does the system security/privacy plan describe actual control implementation?
questions.evidence: Versioned plan and implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: Are common, inherited, hybrid and system-specific responsibilities established?
questions.evidence: Control responsibility and inheritance evidence.

questions.prompt: Does the assessment plan specify methods, objects, depth and coverage?
questions.evidence: Assessment plan and authorized test scope.

questions.prompt: Do identity and access samples support selected control objectives?
questions.evidence: Access-control workpapers and samples.

questions.prompt: Do configuration, vulnerability and change tests address selected controls?
questions.evidence: Technical workpapers and selected populations.

questions.prompt: Are incident response and contingency controls exercised?
questions.evidence: Incident and recovery test records.

questions.prompt: Are findings recorded with evidence, risk, owners and correction plans?
questions.evidence: Assessment findings and action milestones.

questions.prompt: Does continuous monitoring address changing risks and control performance?
questions.evidence: Monitoring strategy and reassessment results.

frameworks.title: NIST SP 800-171
frameworks.scopeNote: Confirm the contractually required revision and CUI boundary. Rev. 3 readiness is not a CMMC assessment or proof of a Rev. 2 contractual requirement.

questions.prompt: Have applicable contracts, CUI categories and required publication revisions been confirmed?
questions.evidence: Contract interpretation and CUI scope determination.

questions.prompt: Are CUI processing, storage, transmission and external connections mapped?
questions.evidence: CUI data flows and system inventory.

questions.prompt: Are security requirements, parameters and implementation responsibilities recorded?
questions.evidence: System security plan and parameter decisions.

questions.prompt: Do access and authentication controls restrict CUI to authorized users?
questions.evidence: Access review and authentication test samples.

questions.prompt: Are audit, monitoring and incident-handling processes effective for CUI systems?
questions.evidence: Logs, alert handling and incident exercises.

questions.prompt: Are configurations, flaws and system changes securely managed?
questions.evidence: Baselines, remediation evidence and change samples.

questions.prompt: Do communications, cryptographic protections and media handling address CUI risks?
questions.evidence: Transport, media and cryptographic evidence.

questions.prompt: Are physical, personnel and supplier dependencies considered?
questions.evidence: Facility, workforce and supplier assurance records.

questions.prompt: Are assessment objectives tested using appropriate evidence and sampling?
questions.evidence: Assessment procedures, workpapers and sample rationale.

questions.prompt: Are remaining deficiencies and ongoing monitoring assigned and tracked?
questions.evidence: Corrective action plan and reassessment records.

frameworks.title: EU NIS2
frameworks.scopeNote: Determine sector, size, jurisdiction, national transposition and implementing rules. Proposed amendments are not treated as enacted obligations.

questions.prompt: Have entity classification, jurisdiction and applicable national requirements been established?
questions.evidence: Applicability analysis and national-law register.

questions.prompt: Are management oversight, approval and cybersecurity competence evidenced?
questions.evidence: Management decisions and training records.

questions.prompt: Are risk analysis and information-system security policies maintained?
questions.evidence: Risk assessments and approved security policies.

questions.prompt: Can incidents be handled and reported through the applicable authority channels?
questions.evidence: Classification procedure and notification exercise.

questions.prompt: Have continuity, backup, recovery and crisis procedures been exercised?
questions.evidence: Continuity plans and exercise outcomes.

questions.prompt: Are direct supplier and service-provider security risks assessed?
questions.evidence: Supplier risk analysis and contractual requirements.

questions.prompt: Are secure acquisition, development and vulnerability handling operational?
questions.evidence: Lifecycle controls and disclosure/remediation records.

questions.prompt: Are control effectiveness and cyber-hygiene practices assessed?
questions.evidence: Effectiveness evaluations and awareness evidence.

questions.prompt: Are cryptography, asset, personnel and access protections appropriate?
questions.evidence: Safeguard decisions and access/configuration tests.

questions.prompt: Are registration, reporting ownership and required records maintained for this jurisdiction?
questions.evidence: Authority contacts, registrations and decision records.

frameworks.title: EU DORA
frameworks.scopeNote: Determine financial-entity scope and applicable technical standards with counsel. Keep national supervisory instructions and proportionality decisions current.

questions.prompt: Are applicability, competent authority and proportionality decisions documented?
questions.evidence: Entity-scope and supervisory-requirements analysis.

questions.prompt: Does management oversee the ICT risk-management framework?
questions.evidence: Governance approvals and accountability records.

questions.prompt: Are ICT assets, dependencies and critical or important functions mapped?
questions.evidence: Function mapping and dependency inventory.

questions.prompt: Are protection, detection and recovery measures tested against ICT risks?
questions.evidence: Technical testing and risk-treatment evidence.

questions.prompt: Can major ICT incidents be classified and reported using applicable requirements?
questions.evidence: Incident classification and reporting exercise.

questions.prompt: Does resilience testing cover relevant systems and remediate identified weaknesses?
questions.evidence: Testing program, results and remediation retests.

questions.prompt: Has applicability of advanced threat-led testing been assessed?
questions.evidence: Scope determination and authorized testing plan.

questions.prompt: Is the register of ICT third-party arrangements complete and maintained?
questions.evidence: Register of information and reconciliation evidence.

questions.prompt: Do ICT contracts, concentration assessments and exit plans address relevant dependencies?
questions.evidence: Contract review, concentration analysis and exit tests.

questions.prompt: Do lessons learned, continuity exercises and regulatory changes update the framework?
questions.evidence: Exercise lessons and framework review decisions.

frameworks.title: FedRAMP Rev5
frameworks.edition: Rev5 agency-authorization path; confirm current eligibility
frameworks.scopeNote: This is advisory preparation for the specifically selected Rev5 path, not FedRAMP Ready, an RAR, an authorization, or a 20x assessment.

questions.prompt: Has the applicable authorization path and current submission eligibility been confirmed?
questions.evidence: Agency/FedRAMP coordination and path decision.

questions.prompt: Are cloud offering boundaries, impact level and service dependencies defined?
questions.evidence: Boundary diagram and impact-level rationale.

questions.prompt: Is agency sponsorship and assessor engagement appropriate to the selected path?
questions.evidence: Agency coordination and recognized-assessor engagement.

questions.prompt: Does the security plan describe selected controls and implementation responsibilities?
questions.evidence: Security plan and responsibility matrix.

questions.prompt: Are federal mandates and applicable technical requirements evidenced?
questions.evidence: Requirement-specific configuration and validation evidence.

questions.prompt: Are inventories, vulnerability scans and remediation processes complete?
questions.evidence: Inventory reconciliation, scans and remediation samples.

questions.prompt: Is the assessment plan agreed with authorized testing boundaries?
questions.evidence: Assessment plan, permissions and sampling approach.

questions.prompt: Are assessment findings and action milestones traceable to evidence?
questions.evidence: Assessment workpapers and corrective-action register.

questions.prompt: Are continuous monitoring, change reporting and incident coordination operational?
questions.evidence: Monitoring submissions and coordination exercise.

questions.prompt: Have advisory gaps been separated from any formal readiness or authorization decision?
questions.evidence: Independent assessor review and decision boundaries.
